text:
Hi! I'm not a programmer, but I'd love a little tool for keeping track of shared costs when I go on trips with friends, so at the end we know who owes whom. Could you make it for me here?

My friend Sam writes scripts and is going to help me hook it up to a spreadsheet, so he wrote down how it should work. He says it should run with the Python that's already on my Mac, without installing anything else, by typing `python3 -m kitty` and a command in this folder, and it should keep everything in a file called `kitty.json` in the folder I run it from.

Here are the commands Sam wrote down:

- `init EUR` starts a new kitty, with EUR (or whatever we're using) as the main currency.
- `member add NAME`, `member remove NAME`, and `member list` for who's in the group.
- `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION` for when someone pays for something. By default it's split equally between everyone, and it should print the expense's ID number. Extras: `--among A,B` to split it equally between only some people; `--exact A=30,B=20`, `--shares A=2,B=1`, or `--percent A=60,B=40` to split it unevenly; `--currency USD` if it was paid in another currency; `--date 2026-07-14` (otherwise it's today); and `--category food` (otherwise "other").
- `expense list` and `expense remove ID`.
- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT` for when someone pays someone else back, also with `--currency` and `--date`.
- `rate set USD 0.92` means one USD is worth 0.92 of the main currency.
- `balances` shows how far up or down each person is overall: positive if they're owed money, negative if they owe.
- `settle` suggests who should pay whom to even everything out.
- `history NAME` lists everything that affected one person, with their running total.
- `report` shows how much each person spent on each category, counting their share of each expense, not what they paid.
- `export FILE` saves the expenses to a CSV file (for the spreadsheet) with the columns id, date, payer, description, amount, currency, category, and base_amount.

Sam also said the reports should print in a format called JSON so his scripts can read them, with money written as text with two decimals, in the main currency unless it's an expense's own amount. His examples:

- `member list`: `["Alice", "Bob"]`
- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`

And if I type something wrong, like a name that isn't in the group or an amount that isn't a number, it should tell me what's wrong and stop (Sam says with "exit status 1"), not crash.

The folder is empty and the Mac has Python 3.9, so I'll write the tool for that version and use only Python's built-in parts.

Every one of Sam's examples comes out exactly right. Next I'll write automated tests for the trickier parts: uneven splits, leftover cents, payments, and settling up with several people.

All 17 tests pass. Last, a short README for you and Sam, and cleaning up my scratch folder:

Your kitty tool is ready in this folder. It runs with the Python already on your Mac, with nothing to install. You type `python3 -m kitty` followed by any of Sam's commands, and it keeps everything in `kitty.json` in the folder you run it from.

I ran Sam's Dinner example, and every report came out exactly matching what he wrote down. I also added 17 automated tests covering the different ways of splitting, other currencies, repayments, settling up with four people, history order, the CSV export and about 30 kinds of typing mistakes. They all pass. Each mistake gets a message like `error: 'Carol' is not in the group (members: Alice, Bob)` and stops with exit status 1, as Sam asked.

To try it:
```
python3 -m kitty init EUR
python3 -m kitty member add Alice
python3 -m kitty member add Bob
python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 45 Dinner at the harbour --category food
python3 -m kitty settle
```
You don't need quotes around descriptions with several words.

Sam's notes left a few details open, so I made these choices. They're also written in `README.md` for Sam:

- **Odd cents:** when an amount doesn't divide evenly, the first people in the list get the extra cent. For example, 10.00 split three ways is 3.34 / 3.33 / 3.33, so the shares always add up to the full amount.
- **Exchange rates:** you have to set a rate (`rate set USD 0.92`) before adding anything in that currency. Each entry keeps the rate in effect when you added it, so changing the rate later doesn't alter past entries.
- **`--exact` amounts** are in the expense's own currency and must add up to the total. `--percent` values must add up to 100.
- **Removing a member** only works if they have no expenses or payments yet, so the balances stay correct.
- **`init` won't overwrite** an existing kitty. Use a separate folder for each trip.
- **Messages:** most commands print a short confirmation like "Added Alice." `expense add` prints just the ID number, as Sam specified.

**One gap:** Sam's list has no way to view or undo a repayment. If you record one by mistake, you'd currently have to edit `kitty.json` by hand. I can add `payment list` and `payment remove` if you'd like.

Thanks, this sounds great! Those choices mostly match what I had in mind. Just to check a couple:

- Odd cents: the "first people in the list" should be the order I typed them with --among, or the order they joined the group if it's split between everyone. Shares and percentages work the same way: everyone gets their part rounded down to the cent, and the extra cents go one each in the order I listed them. So 10.00 with --shares A=1,B=2 should be A 3.34, B 6.66.
- Exchange rates: when converting, round to the cent with halves going up, so 0.125 becomes 0.13 and never 0.12. It should also refuse a rate for the main currency itself.

And yes, please add payment list and payment remove. That would be handy.

I made both changes and added payment list and payment remove. All 21 tests pass.

**Odd cents:** I had to change how this works. Before, the extra cent went to whoever lost the most to rounding, so `10.00 --shares A=1,B=2` gave A 3.33 and B 6.67. Now it follows your rule: everyone's part is rounded down to the cent, then the extra cents go one each in the order you listed people. With an even split between everyone, it's the order they joined the group. That example now gives A 3.34 and B 6.66, and `--among C,B,A` gives C the extra cent. This only affects expenses added from now on; any you've already added keep their old shares.

**Exchange rates:** this already worked the way you described, so nothing changed. Converted amounts round halves up (0.25 USD at 0.5 becomes 0.13), and `rate set EUR 1` is refused when EUR is the main currency. I added tests to make sure it stays that way.

**Payments:**
- `payment list` shows all repayments: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-15", "from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.00", "currency": "EUR", "base_amount": "20.00"}]`
- `payment remove ID` deletes one, and balances, settle and history update to match.
- **Change for Sam:** `payment add` now prints the new payment's ID number, the same way `expense add` does, so you know which number to remove. Before, it printed a sentence.
- ID numbers are never reused after a removal. Any kitty you've already started will number its existing payments automatically.

I've updated `README.md` with all of this so Sam has it.
